verdict.rationale: Bugbot's docs say it reads existing top-level and inline PR comments to avoid duplicate suggestions, and Cursor reports an 80% resolution rate even at high effort, which signals low false positives. One community user says almost none of its comments are frivolous or wrong. Against that, another user saw it re-raise a recommendation they had just reverted, and someone else turned off automatic reviews because of verbose comment history. missing for 10: any documented severity labels or priority levels on findings, independent false-positive metrics, and consistent deduplication across review cycles.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, the reviewer keeps noise low — few false positives, deduplicated comments, severity labels — so my team doesn't tune it out

citations.quote: reads connected PR comments (top-level and inline) to avoid duplicate suggestions and build on prior feedback
Bugbot with high effort finds 35% more bugs while resolution rate stays constant at 80%.
almost none of its comments are frivolous or wrong, and it finds genuine bugs most reviewers miss
